Variants.Content: The Chiheda family belongs to the old blood class of Volantis, and the political significance of the family name comes from the blood qualifications within the Black Wall. The real power of the family must still fall on real estate, cargo, manors, debts and kinship alliances; in a city where the consul is elected, noble birth also requires business support. The Tiger vs. Elephant debate cuts through every Old Blood family, and Chiheda cannot forever avoid the choice between war interests, trade security, and the slave order. True reputation is accumulated by choices and their costs.

When the Blackwall nobles observe Qiheda, they will judge the direction by which family it intermarries with and which candidate it supports. Volantis politics has no permanent friends, only relationships that will be recalculated by the next election.

Ordinary free people hope that old blood families like Chiheda will talk less about their ancestors and more about bridge taxes, food prices and street security. Ballots are one of the few moments when they can make the characters behind the black walls lean in and listen.

Entry Qihda Chiheda is one of the Old Blood Houses of the Volantis, whose status is embedded in Blackwall bloodlines, business holdings, slavery, and electoral alliances. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
